I don't have any notes for you yet. My research tool stopped working before I could read a single page, so I can't write the verse-by-verse notes on Jeremiah 24.

My first attempt to load the pages crashed because of a bug in my code. When I tried again, the tool told me I'd used up my calls for this turn. Nothing from Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes) or Precept Austin came back. You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, so I haven't filled any verse from memory.

If you reply "continue," I'll start over and keep my code to a minimum so it doesn't run out again. These are the sources I'd read:

- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word (Jeremiah 24), Bible Hub's Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes and Benson commentaries, Precept Austin, and StudyLight.
- **Differences between traditions:** Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Ligonier, Desiring God and Grace to You (gty.org), Lutheran sources (lcms.org, 1517.org), and Anglican readings such as Ryle where they exist. Verse 7 ("I will give them a heart to know Me") is the likeliest place for real disagreement. It bears on grace and conversion, which Reformed and Wesleyan teachers handle differently.
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship, and New Advent (the Church Fathers and the Catholic Encyclopedia) and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings. I'll include any popular modern teachings on this chapter only if the allowed sites actually discuss them.
